content:
incident-bot: ALERT: prod-us-west-2 streaming p99 latency > 5s for last 10m. SLO breach triggered. Auto-escalating to on-call.
alice_oncall: saw it. paging oncall now. p95 creeping too. reassigning to SRE. @bob_sre you're on the incident.
bob_sre: on it. initial glance: p95 ~ 820ms (baseline ~250-300ms), p99 ~ 5.2s. streaming endpoints showing mid-stream stalls + reconnects. will pull logs.
ella_support: getting multiple customer reports of truncated/paused streams, some missed tokens. Marking potential customer-impact. Customers affected: two enterprise orgs + handful of free-tier sessions.
carol_runtime: FYI we pushed prefix-hash v2 at 16:10 UTC (~2h ago) to improve namespace salting. Could be related. I've seen a cache key format change in that deploy.
bob_sre: ok hypothesis: new prefix-hash changed cache key => widespread low cache hit-rate => backend cold reads => tail latency spike. Can we check cache hit metrics?
carol_runtime: query run:
```
SELECT 1 - sum(misses)/sum(requests) as hit_rate
FROM cache_metrics
WHERE cluster='prod-us-west-2' AND window='1h'
```
results: hit_rate dropped from 0.92 -> 0.18 after 16:10 UTC.
dan_platform: confirmed eviction storm and higher backend QPS. Some paging latencies hitting p99 db calls. We're seeing sustained backend CPU saturation on model-io nodes.
bob_sre: this matches. Streaming stalls are likely because many streaming connections hit a cold KV path and block on disk reads or remote model loading.
alice_oncall: what's the blast radius? any single-customer SLO breaches?
ella_support: two enterprise customers reported degraded SLAs. I've flagged both and started a priority support thread.
frank_pm: customers flagged in support thread A-12345 and B-9876. Need a quick mitigation + proactive outreach plan.
carol_runtime: mitigation options: 1) revert prefix-hash v2 rollout (fast) 2) enable fallback key generation to old hash for 60m 3) ramp up cache warmers for top prefixes (pre-warm) 4) throttle new streaming sessions temporarily.
bob_sre: immediate plan: revert rollout to v1 to restore hit-rate; while rollback in progress, enable temporary throttling to reduce queueing. Then run warmup job for top 1k prefixes.
alice_oncall: agree. Rollback steps? Keep me posted on commands.
carol_runtime: executing rollback (canary already paused). Command:
```
# revert prefix-hash feature flag
redwoodctl feature-flag set prefix-hash-v2 false --env prod-us-west-2 --scope rollout
# validate
redwoodctl rollout status prefix-hash --env prod-us-west-2
```
carol_runtime: started the revert now. canary halted @ 16:45 UTC.
bob_sre: while that's rolling back, applying throttling rule to streaming route to limit concurrent tokens per connection:
```
routectl set-rate-limit --route streaming.v1 --concurrency 4 --burst 8
```
dan_platform: also increased cache thread-pool on model-io nodes temporarily and added a short TTL override so caches treat warmed keys as sticky for 5m.
carol_runtime: rollback completed at 16:58 UTC. metrics: cache hit-rate recovering: 0.18 -> 0.67 in the first 5m.
bob_sre: nice. streaming p99 down to ~1.2s now. p95 ~350ms. still a bit higher than baseline but trending down.
ella_support: customers A & B acknowledged we reached out and are monitoring. No data loss reported, mostly latency/interrupts. They've accepted temporary mitigation update.
frank_pm: good work. timeframe to full recovery?
carol_runtime: running cache warmup for top prefixes now (script below). This should hit 90%+ in ~20m for steady prefixes.
```
# warmup top prefixes
python tools/warmup.py --top 1000 --env prod-us-west-2 --parallel 32
```
bob_sre: monitoring query to keep an eye on tail latencies:
```
SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 95), percentile(latency_ms, 99)
FROM streaming_requests
WHERE region='us-west-2' AND window='5m'
```
set alert if p99 > 2s.
alice_oncall: I'm going to mute noisy alerts and update incident channel to reduce signal. @incident-bot please annotate incident with rollback action and owner.
incident-bot: Incident annotated: 'rollback prefix-hash-v2' by carol_runtime. severity -> sev2.
dan_platform: backend CPU pressure easing. cache hit-rate at 0.81 after 12m. p99 now 420ms. Looks like warmups are effective.
bob_sre: confirming streaming stalls largely gone. leaving throttling for another 10m then remove.
carol_runtime: removing throttling in 10m. will keep an eye on sudden re-spike.
ella_support: re-opened support tickets with notes. adding post-incident comms draft: will notify impacted customers with timeline + mitigation.
alice_oncall: handoff in 30m to night oncall (bob_night). Summary: prefix-hash v2 rollout caused cache key incompatibility => hit-rate collapse => backend paging/cold loads => p99 spike & streaming stalls. Mitigation: immediate rollback to v1, temp throttling, cache warmup, increased cache threads. Current state: recovering, p99 back to baseline. Postmortem owner: frank_pm. Next steps: add rollout check to CI (cache-compat smoke), add automated prewarm for prefix-key churns, improve alert to tie hit-rate drops to deploys.
frank_pm: acknowledged. I'll create the postmortem doc and ship action items. Assigning follow-ups to carol_runtime (rollout safety), dan_platform (warmup infra), bob_sre (alert tuning), ella_support (customer comms).
alice_oncall: handing off to bob_night in 30m. Please keep slack updates minimal unless we see regressions.
bob_sre: on standby for night shift. added myself to incident thread as secondary.
carol_runtime: leaving logs + traces in incident folder: /infra/incidents/1710574321/artifacts.tar.gz
ella_support: adding communication snippet to support thread. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: status -> monitoring. last update logged 17:20 UTC."
